tree.notes: Starfish (5-armed sea star) read from the side (XY) view, which shows the classic star silhouette (one arm up, two lateral, two lower-diagonal). The front (ZY) and top (XZ) views show the arms collapsing toward the central disc when projected along the axis they lie in, confirming the arms lie essentially flat in the XY plane (world Z ~ 0) and the small central bulge visible in those two views is just the disc's thickness, not an arm. Each arm was split into a 'base' (hub) segment of length 4, matching the observed central-disc radius, and a longer 'tip' segment carrying the remainder of the arm to its point - this 2-segment split is an inferred joint (no true joint exists anatomically, but the protocol requires multi-segment limbs). Left/Right arms and Lower-left/Lower-right arms are treated as symmetric pairs with equal total length (12 and 13 respectively); the single top arm has no mirror partner. Root 'center' represents the middle of the central disc, length 0, direction [0,0,0]. Only the 5 arm tips count as leaves (one per ray), per the leaf-convention rule.

Root placed at mesosoma/body core (13,15 in side-view grid). +x world = forward/toward head = decreasing side-view x (side view has head at low x, tail at high x; top view is mirrored left-right relative to side view, so top-view x was used only for confirming lateral z-spread, not for world-x sign). +y world = up = decreasing image-y. +z world = animal's left, assigned arbitrarily to the "positive" image-lateral direction in top/front views; right-side limbs mirror the sign, which is the only requirement since the pairs are symmetric.

Inferred splits (anatomical inference, not directly labeled): (1) Metasoma (tail) divided into 4 tapering segments + telson based on the 4 visible curvature bends in the side view (17,15)->(20,13)->(21,9)->(19,6)->telson(18,7). (2) Each pedipalp (claw arm) split into base/arm/claw (coxa+trochanter / humerus+brachium / chela), inferred since only the overall envelope (cephalothorax joint to claw tip) and lateral claw spread (top view z=4/z=20) were directly readable; a single straight direction was used for all three segments as a simplification (pose of the elbow bend not encoded, per "proportion not pose"). (3) Each of the 8 walking legs split into thigh/knee/shank/hock/foot (5-segment simplification of the true 7-segment arachnid leg), with identical segment-length proportions (3,3,3,1,1) across all four leg pairs per instruction #3 (equal proportions despite mid-stride pose differences in the render); only the base direction's fore/aft lean differs per pair to reflect attachment position along the body, using a single straight direction per leg (no distinct bend at each joint) as a proportional simplification. Lateral (z) magnitudes for legs and claws were inferred by combining the side-view x/y reach with the front/top-view lateral spread (~z=3 to z=21 about a body centerline of z=12), since no single view gives full 3-D reach directly.
